response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-12

CLINICAL INDICATION: Routine surveillance. History of treated breast cancer. No new symptoms.

ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. L. Okafor (synthetic), medical oncology

COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-02-10

TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Both studies are adequate and comparable. Differences from prior: current has slightly deeper inspiration, with the right dome projecting a little lower. Current has slightly greater penetration and contrast. Shoulder, arm and breast position differ, and the left chest device projects higher on current.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F2: right lower zone interstitial finding (indeterminate). Not marked time-sensitive.
- F1: device finding (indeterminate, reads disagreed). Not marked time-sensitive.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central, no narrowing seen. Lungs well expanded. No consolidation, mass or collapse. Linear bronchovascular markings are mildly prominent in the medial right lower zone, with a single small dense nodular focus projected among them (F2, indeterminate). Left lung clear. Apices clear.
- Mediastinum / hila: Prominent rounded aortic knuckle, consistent with an unfolded aorta (F3). Upper mediastinum not widened. Hila normal in position, with no one-sided hilar enlargement.
- Pleura: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax. Both costophrenic angles sharp. No pleural thickening.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette not enlarged on PA view (F4). Borders distinct.
- Bones / soft tissue: No rib, clavicle or shoulder fracture or destructive lesion seen at this resolution. Visible spine aligned. Bilateral breast shadows. No soft tissue gas.
- Devices (F1, indeterminate): The two blind reads disagreed (one read stable, the other indeterminate). The finding entry describes external monitoring leads projecting over the chest on one film, with no implanted device identified. The systematic read describes thin tubing across the left upper zone consistent with an implanted venous access port and catheter. The catheter tip is not traced over the mediastinum. The same configuration is present on both studies and projects higher on current, in keeping with different arm and breast position. No kink or discontinuity seen at this resolution.
- Below diaphragm: Both domes well defined. Gastric bubble and gas-filled bowel loops under the left dome. No free gas under the diaphragm.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: F2, medial right lower zone. Markings are more conspicuous on current, and the small nodular focus is not clearly seen on prior. This is indeterminate, because the current film is more penetrated with higher contrast, which might explain the appearance. A measurement was supplied for F2: 12 mm on prior, 13 mm on current. The bases for this measurement and its relation to the described nodular focus should be confirmed on the source images.
- Unchanged: Aortic knuckle prominence (F3) is similar on both studies. Cardiac silhouette (F4) is not enlarged on either film and is similar. Lungs otherwise, pleura and mediastinal contour are without definite change. The device configuration (F1) is the same on both studies, but the reads disagreed, so this is indeterminate.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the small dense focus in the medial right lower zone a true lung nodule, and is it new? | Reason: The focus is small and lies among vessels, so a vessel seen end-on or a calcified granuloma cannot be separated from a nodule on a frontal film. The softer exposure of the prior may hide it. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If it persists, CT chest.
- Have the right lower zone lung markings truly increased since the prior? (F2) | Reason: The current study is more penetrated with higher contrast, which makes fine markings more conspicuous without a real change. | Recommend: Review source images side by side in PACS with matched windowing. Interval follow-up PA film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Where is the tip of the left-sided venous catheter? (F1) | Reason: The thin catheter cannot be followed over the dense mediastinal shadow on these low-resolution frontal images. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with edge-enhanced windowing, or obtain a lateral view.
- Where is the tip of the left-sided venous catheter, and has it moved? (F1) | Reason: The catheter is lost over the dense mediastinal shadow on both films at this resolution. The chest wall component projects at a different rib level on the two films. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with window adjustment. Add a lateral view if tip position matters clinically.
- Is the tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on current a nodule, a vessel end-on or a calcified granuloma, and is it new? | Reason: The focus is too small for a frontal X-ray to separate a nodule from a vessel end-on or a bone island. On prior the same area is covered by breast shadow on a lower contrast film. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS. CT chest if it persists or is of clinical concern.
- Are the more conspicuous right lower zone markings on current a real interval change? (F2) | Reason: Breast shadow overlap, contrast and depth of inspiration differ between the two films. | Recommend: Correlate clinically. Repeat PA and lateral with matched technique, or CT chest if concern persists.
- Are the faint linear densities lateral to the left hilum on prior a real band of atelectasis or scarring, and have they cleared? | Reason: Mild rotation and lower contrast on prior. Vessels and the overlying catheter cross the same area. The appearance is not reproduced on current. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. No further imaging needed if the radiologist confirms normal vessels.
- Is there a subtle rib, spine or shoulder lesion? | Reason: The low resolution, compressed image limits fine bone detail. Shoulders and ribs are partly overlapped by soft tissue. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings. Dedicated imaging if there is focal pain or clinical concern.

IMPRESSION:
1. Indeterminate small dense nodular focus with more conspicuous linear markings in the medial right lower zone (F2), not clearly seen on prior. Exposure and contrast differences may account for the appearance. A measurement of 12 mm on prior and 13 mm on current was supplied. Cannot determine whether this is a true nodule or whether it is new. Needs review of the source images in a patient with prior breast cancer.
2. Device finding (F1) is indeterminate, because the two blind reads disagreed. The same configuration is seen on both studies, and the catheter tip cannot be traced.
3. No mass, pleural effusion, hilar or mediastinal enlargement, or destructive bone lesion at this resolution.
4. Prominent aortic knuckle (F3) and non-enlarged cardiac silhouette (F4), similar to prior.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review the source images in PACS (F2 and F1) with matched windowing and bone settings as needed.
- CT chest if the right lower zone focus persists on source review or there is clinical concern (interval not specified in the findings).
- Lateral view if catheter tip position matters clinically.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
